as_of.observation_horizon: current conditions through next-year contract talks

input.raw_text: Spot rates across the major east-west trades are close to ten times pre-pandemic levels, and even that understates the panic: five figures for a forty-foot box out of Asia, whatever the destination. Off Los Angeles and Long Beach the queue has smashed every record, more than seventy vessels at anchor, and congestion inland means boxes never seem to come back. Every link of the chain is broken at once, from terminal labor to chassis and yard space, with equipment stranded wherever the pandemic left it. Carriers are blanking nothing; sailings are full weeks out and Golden Week brings no relief because the capacity simply is not there. Next year's contract talks are starting and shippers are capitulating to almost any number to secure space. The lines are printing record profits and nothing on the horizon unblocks this.
input.summary: Container shipping remains under extreme strain, with spot rates near ten times prepandemic levels, record vessel queues at Los Angeles and Long Beach, inland congestion, displaced equipment, and shortages across terminals, chassis, and yard capacity. Sailings remain fully booked weeks ahead, seasonal effects offer no meaningful relief, and shippers are accepting sharply higher contract rates to secure capacity. Carrier profitability is at record levels, while no near-term normalization catalyst is evident.

interpretation.summary: The candidate set does not represent the observed container-shipping strain. Its states describe financial return dynamics, correlation structures, volatility regimes, or traded-market liquidity, while the packet evidences physical logistics congestion and capacity scarcity.

observations.statement: Spot rates near ten times prepandemic levels
Five-figure Asia-origin container rates across destinations
Record queue exceeding seventy vessels off Los Angeles and Long Beach
Slow container returns caused by inland congestion
Simultaneous constraints in labor, chassis, yard space, and equipment positioning
Sailings fully booked weeks ahead despite continued carrier deployment
No meaningful Golden Week capacity relief
Shipper acceptance of sharply higher contract rates to secure space
